A1.justification: Both PDFs describe the same IBISAgent work and contain readable main text and Appendices A-F. Full-text and rendered-page comparisons support reliable matching of the methods, equations, tables, and figures.

before.justification: v3 reports original segmentation, VQA, efficiency, and ablation results in Section 4 and Appendix D.

after.justification: v4 retains the original segmentation, VQA, efficiency, and ablation results in Section 4 and Appendix D.

M1.justification: The iterative reasoning-click-observation procedure, segmentation tool integration, cold-start SFT, self-reflection training, and GRPO reward design are unchanged. Edits to their descriptions do not establish procedural changes.

E1.justification: Both versions retain the same training corpora, three segmentation evaluation datasets, medical VQA evaluations, and error-correction scenarios. Appendix A's modality and task coverage is unchanged.

E2.justification: Comparator membership is unchanged in Tables 1-3 and 8-10. UniBiomed also remains in Figure 9's pancreatic-tumor comparison through its textual response, despite removal of its displayed mask.

E3.justification: Section 4.1 and the appendices retain the same splits, metrics, Qwen2.5-VL-7B backbone, training budgets, baseline fine-tuning arrangements, and testing procedures. No new evaluation protocol is introduced.

E4.justification: The pancreatic-tumor case study in Figure 9 loses the visual evidence of UniBiomed's incorrect mask. Training and reward ablations, segmentation-tool analyses, error-correction examples, and RL dynamics otherwise remain unchanged.

E5.justification: Neither version adds repeated-run counts, seeds, confidence intervals, or significance testing. The existing descriptive statistics, including the training-curve summaries in Figure 13, are unchanged.

E6.justification: Numerical results are unchanged, including Table 1's IBISAgent IoUs of 85.58, 80.63, and 72.09. The limited result removal is UniBiomed's mask image in Figure 9; its textual response and the caption's incorrect-mask finding remain.

T1.justification: Equations 1-14 retain the same rollout, optimization, trajectory-generation, and reward definitions. No formal assumptions, derivations, theorems, or proofs are added or revised.

C1.justification: The shortened abstract preserves the claims of iterative pixel-level reasoning, segmentation without architectural modifications, two-stage training, and superior performance. The introduction's contribution list and conclusion retain their scientific scope.

C2.justification: Mechanism explanations and substantive qualifications remain the same, including potential training-test overlap, the inference-cost tradeoff, and the primarily 2D scope discussed in Appendix F. Local sentence deletions condense existing explanations.

D1.justification: v3 promises future public release of datasets, code, and trained models. v4 replaces this with a first-page repository link stating that code and trained models are available, without retaining the explicit dataset-release promise. Repository contents cannot be verified from the PDFs; implementation details otherwise remain unchanged.

R1.justification: The same 46 references and research positioning are retained. Section 3.3 adds an inline citation to the already-cited BiomedParseData work, without introducing a new cited work or changing the relationship to prior research.

P1.justification: v4 condenses the abstract and several introductory, method, and setup passages, corrects some wording, and adds affiliations and funding acknowledgments. The section sequence and most prose, especially the appendices, remain unchanged.

P2.justification: Figures 2-3 receive label and icon edits, Figure 9 omits the UniBiomed mask image, and Tables 4-5 are repositioned within page 8. Text reflows across pages, while most appendix pages render identically.

improvement.justification: The concrete code/model access link modestly improves reproducibility documentation over v3's future-release promise, and some prose becomes more concise. These gains are limited: the scientific methods and numerical evidence remain unchanged, Figure 9 loses support for its retained incorrect-mask claim, and the explicit dataset-release promise disappears. The overall benefit concerns documented access and usability, not verified repository completeness or stronger experimental evidence.
